reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space with its Borel measurable structure and canonical ordinary Lebesgue volume; dimension zero is allowed and all approved ambient section instances are part of the contract. Let v,F:E->R, G:E->E and K:Set E. Assume K is compact and each of tsupport(v), tsupport(F), tsupport(G) is contained in K. Assume actual MemLp v 2 volume, MemLp F 2 volume and MemLp G 2 volume; these include volume-a.e. strong measurability and finite L2 norm.
Assume that for every real C1 compactly supported psi:E->R and every a:E, both x->psi(x)*<G(x),a>_E and x->v(x)*(fderiv R psi x a) are volume-integrable and
  integral psi(x)*<G(x),a>_E dx = - integral v(x)*(fderiv R psi x a) dx.
Assume also that for every real C2 compactly supported psi:E->R, both x->v(x)*Delta(psi)(x) and x->F(x)*psi(x) are volume-integrable and
  integral v(x)*Delta(psi)(x) dx = integral F(x)*psi(x) dx.
The test Laplacian is the actual finite-basis trace. No pointwise classical derivatives of v or G or F, Sobolev certificate, core theorem, or sequence certificate are premises.
Then there exist a compact set Kprime in E and one sequence phi:N->SchwartzMap E R such that, for every n, tsupport(phi_n) is contained in Kprime, and the actual scalar quotient classes (phi_n).toLp 2 volume converge as n tends to infinity to hv2.toLp(v) in the norm topology of scalar L2(volume). There further exists a family hphiG of actual MemLp witnesses, one for each n, for gradient(phi_n):E->E at exponent 2 with respect to volume, such that the same sequence's actual vector quotient classes (hphiG_n).toLp(gradient(phi_n)) converge in vector L2(volume) norm to hG2.toLp(G), and the same sequence's scalar quotient classes (Delta(phi_n)).toLp 2 volume converge in scalar L2(volume) norm to hF2.toLp(F).
All three limits are Filter.Tendsto atTop (nhds the displayed actual quotient target). The MemLp.toLp targets are volume-a.e. linked to the original pointwise inputs. The Schwartz functions are genuine smooth rapidly decreasing real functions on real E, and their classical gradients and Laplacians are actual operators on these smooth approximants. This is one common compact Kprime and one sequence for all n and for all three limits, not three separate sequences or moving n-dependent support sets. There is no containment relation asserted between Kprime and K, no rate, no pointwise convergence, no support equality for chosen quotient representatives, and no weighted-domain/core or further inequality/composition conclusion.
objects: Real pointwise v,F and vector G; compact K bounding their three topological supports; actual volume-L2 quotient targets hv2.toLp v,hF2.toLp F,hG2.toLp G; C1 ordinary weak-gradient and C2 weak-Poisson tests; one compact Kprime and one real Schwartz sequence phi; genuine approximant gradient and Laplacian; explicit universal gradient MemLp proof family hphiG and actual gradient quotient embeddings.
domains: Finite-dimensional real Hilbert Borel E and canonical ordinary volume, including dimension zero and approved section instances. v,F:E->R,G:E->E,K/Kprime:Set E. All MemLp and L1 products use actual volume. Functions and Laplacians converge in scalar Lp R 2 volume, gradients in vector Lp E 2 volume, all genuine quotient norm topologies; no local or pointwise convergence interpretation. phi:N->SchwartzMap E R consists of actual smooth rapidly decreasing real functions whose supports lie in one compact Kprime.
quantifiers: Universally over approved ambient E,v,F,G,K satisfying all premises. Weak gradient is forall real C1 compact psi and forall a:E; weak Poisson is forall real C2 compact psi. Exists Kprime, compact Kprime, exists one phi sequence, then forall n support containment and scalar-function limit; exists hphiG:forall n gradient MemLp2 volume, with the vector-gradient limit and scalar-Laplacian limit for that same sequence. The three targets are the actual input MemLp.toLp classes. Kprime and sequence precede all n/limits, not distinct choices per derivative component.
assumptions: K IsCompact; tsupport v,tsupport F,tsupport G each subset K; actual MemLp v/F/G 2 volume. For every C1 compact real psi and a:E, both psi*<G,a> and v*Dpsi[a] are volume-integrable and integral psi*<G,a>=-integral v*Dpsi[a]. For every C2 compact real psi, both v*Delta psi and F*psi are volume-integrable and integral v*Delta psi=integral F*psi. No Sobolev, sequence or core input certificate; no classical regularity assumption on rough v,F,G.
conclusion: Exists common compact Kprime and single genuine real Schwartz sequence with all supports contained in Kprime; phi_n.toLp2volume converges to hv2.toLp(v), actual gradient classes from explicit hphiG_n MemLp witnesses converge to hG2.toLp(G), and actual Laplacian classes converge to hF2.toLp(F), each atTop in the corresponding genuine L2 norm topology. All three simultaneous limits use the same sequence and actual AE-linked inputs.
scopes: Compact-support/L1/PDE/L2 assertions about inputs are premises, not outputs or wrappers around an assumed sequence. One Kprime works for all n and the same phi serves all three limits. Kprime is not required to contain K; selected quotient representatives are not given pointwise support identities. No approximation rate, weighted-domain/core certification, pointwise convergence or classical rough-function Laplacian conclusion. Ordinary-volume graph approximation alone is not a further functional inequality or kernel-composition certificate.
constant_dependencies: All L2 exponents exactly 2; gradient equation minus sign and Poisson equality positive sign with unit coefficients. No numerical rate or estimate constant. Kprime,phi and gradient proof family may depend on input v,F,G,K and their premises, but do not change with n or among the three limits. Dimension may be zero; no support-radius relation or separation between Kprime and K is supplied.
